items.title: Nepal's prime minister makes first official visit to India
items.what_happened: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah visited New Delhi on 22 and 23 November. He held talks with Prime Minister Modi and the two sides announced aid, energy and transport projects.
confirmed_facts: The visit ran from 22 to 23 November 2026, with talks at Hyderabad House on 23 November, ETV Bharat reported.
India announced a reconstruction package after Nepal's August 2026 floods, according to ETV Bharat's live coverage.
The sides adopted a 10-pillar joint vision with a monitoring group that meets at least every six months, ETV Bharat reported.
A road bridge linking Dharchula and Darchula opened and a weekly Ayodhya to Janakpur train was flagged off, ETV Bharat reported.
items.why_it_matters: Nepal is a key neighbour for India's energy, trade and border security. The visit signals a reset after a tense period with Nepal's new government.
items.context: Shah's government came to power after the 2025 youth protests. Earlier in 2026 his aides said he would not travel abroad in his first year, and a border dispute over Lipulekh resurfaced.
items.analysis: Big project and aid packages are India's main tool to keep influence in Nepal as China also competes there. Delivery speed will decide whether the goodwill lasts.
items.uncertainty: Reports differ on the size of the aid package. The Lipulekh border dispute was not publicly settled.
items.what_to_watch: Whether the package size is confirmed, the first meeting of the monitoring group, and progress on the 669 MW Lower Arun hydro project.

items.title: RBI proposes new customer controls against digital payment fraud
items.what_happened: The Reserve Bank of India issued draft rules on 23 November to protect electronic banking from fraud. Reports say it dropped an earlier idea of a one-hour delay on larger transfers.
confirmed_facts: The RBI listed draft amendment directions on preventive safeguards for electronic banking transactions dated 23 November 2026.
DNP India reported a proposed stop switch that lets customers block all outgoing debits at once.
Customers could name a trusted person to approve transfers above a set limit, DNP India reported.
DNP India said the April 2026 idea of a one-hour cooling period for transfers of Rs 10,000 or more was dropped.
items.why_it_matters: Digital payments are central to daily life in India, and fraud losses are rising. These rules could change how millions of people use UPI and net banking.
items.context: In April 2026 the RBI floated a discussion paper with a cooling period and a kill switch. The new draft follows public feedback on that paper.
items.analysis: Most tools are opt-in, so the benefit depends on banks making them easy to find and on customers turning them on.
items.uncertainty: The RBI listing gives only the title. Details come from one news report and may change in the final rules.
items.what_to_watch: Final rules after the 14 December comment deadline. Reported start dates are 1 January 2027 for bank liability rules and 1 July 2027 for customer controls.

items.title: COP31 climate talks in Turkey end without a deal
items.what_happened: The UN climate summit in Antalya ended on 22 November with no agreed final decision. The EU and many others rejected a text that did not call for moving away from fossil fuels.
confirmed_facts: The talks ran about two days past the planned 20 November close, IntelliNews and The Hindu reported.
The Hindu said over 130 parties, led by the EU, rejected the draft cover text.
India and China accepted the text to move talks forward, IntelliNews reported. The Hindu also named Saudi Arabia as a supporter.
COP31 President Murat Kurum said he would not put forward a new text, The Hindu reported.
items.why_it_matters: It is the first collapse of this kind since Copenhagen in 2009. It weakens global climate action and leaves finance and fossil fuel questions open.
items.context: India went to Antalya pressing rich countries to meet their climate finance duties under the Paris Agreement. It stressed equity and differentiated responsibilities.
items.analysis: The split puts India on the opposite side from the EU and small island states on fossil fuel wording. That could shape trade talks, including over carbon border taxes.
items.uncertainty: Accounts differ on exactly which countries backed or blocked the text. Some technical decisions may still be counted as adopted.
items.what_to_watch: How leftover items are handled at the Bonn session in June 2027, and whether India updates its climate plans before COP32.

items.title: Bangladesh tensions rise over Sheikh Hasina's planned return from India
items.what_happened: Bangladesh says it will arrest former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina if she returns from India. She has vowed to come back in December, and unrest has grown.
confirmed_facts: Hasina has lived in India since fleeing in August 2024 and was sentenced to death in absentia, AFP reported.
Bangladesh deployed border guard forces in seven districts after arson and violence, AFP reported on 19 November.
Dhaka police said 107 people linked to the Awami League were arrested, AFP reported.
On 23 November a Bangladeshi minister said Hasina would be arrested on return, according to a Reuters report summarised by Just Security.
items.why_it_matters: The issue directly affects India, which hosts Hasina and has an extradition request from Dhaka. A return could trigger more violence near India's border.
items.context: The Awami League is banned. A new government led by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman took office in February 2026.
items.analysis: India faces a hard choice between ties with Dhaka's new government and its long links with Hasina.
items.uncertainty: No exact return date has been confirmed. It is unclear whether India will let her travel or act on the extradition request.
items.what_to_watch: Any announced return date, India's response, and further unrest or arrests in December.

items.title: Russia-Ukraine war spreads far beyond the front line
items.what_happened: Over 21 to 23 November, Russian strikes hit Ukrainian towns while Ukraine said it struck Russian ships as far away as Libya. Poland reported a Russian airspace violation.
confirmed_facts: Zelenskyy said Ukraine sank a Russian corvette near Libya's coast, a Reuters report summarised by Just Security said.
The Kremlin accused Ukraine of terrorism after a drone hit a Russian cargo ship in the Baltic, Just Security reported citing Reuters.
NATO chief Mark Rutte pledged to defend all Polish territory after the reported violation, Just Security reported.
US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi earlier in November gave no breakthrough beyond a prisoner swap deal, Al Jazeera reported.
items.why_it_matters: Attacks at sea raise risks for global shipping and energy. They also raise the chance of a direct clash between Russia and NATO.
items.context: Earlier in November Ukraine hit a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland and a Baltic port. The US has criticised such strikes over fuel prices.
items.analysis: Both sides seem to be using force to gain leverage while peace talks continue.
items.uncertainty: Several claims come from the warring parties and are hard to verify independently.
items.what_to_watch: The next round of peace talks, any NATO response to Poland's report, and more strikes on shipping.

notes: Reuters and BBC pages could not be opened. Bangladesh and Ukraine items use Just Security's digest of Reuters and AP. The Hindu items come via a summary page. RBI details come from one news report plus the RBI listing.
